# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 2 (EMET Literal)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 2
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Since therefore the days are evil and the working one himself possesses the power of this present age, we ought to attend to ourselves and to seek out the righteous ordinances of the Lord.
2. The helpers of our faith are fear and patience, and our allies are long-suffering and self-control.
3. When these things remain pure with respect to the Lord, wisdom, understanding, science, and knowledge rejoice together with them.
4. For he has made clear to us through all the prophets that he needs neither sacrifices nor whole burnt-offerings nor general offerings, saying at one time:
5. "What to me is the multitude of your sacrifices? says the Lord. I am full of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fed lambs; and I delight not in the blood of bulls and goats and male goats, not even when you come to appear before me. For who required these things from your hands?
6. You shall no more tread my court. If you bring fine flour, it is vain; incense is an abomination to me; your new moons and sabbaths I cannot bear.
7. These things therefore he has cancelled, so that the new law of our Lord Jesus Christ, being without the yoke of constraint, may have its human offering.
8. And again he says to them: "Did I command your fathers when they came out from the land of Egypt to bring me burnt offerings and sacrifices?
9. But this I commanded them: Let none of you bear malice in his heart against his neighbor, and love not a false oath."
10. We ought then to have understanding, if we are not without sense, of the gracious intention of our Father; for he speaks to us, wishing that we should not go astray like them and seek how we may make a gift to him.
11. To us therefore he says this: "A sacrifice to God is a broken heart; a smell of sweet savor to the Lord is a heart that glorifies him who made it. For brothers, we ought to take heed concerning our salvation, lest the evil one should slip in with error and should hurl us away from our life."
